title: Go client: response shape factories and stream ingress helpers
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Implement a set of composable, strongly typed helpers in the Go SDK to simplify decoding structured outputs from streaming responses and to provide a robust ingress path for stream-based APIs. This ticket focuses on: 1) response shape factories that produce typed structs with lightweight validation hooks, 2) a StreamIngress layer that normalizes retries, resume tokens, and context cancellation across HTTP/GRPC streaming, and 3) example integrations and test harnesses demonstrating ergonomic usage patterns (CLI example, small server + client test). The goal is to reduce customer boilerplate when consuming structured outputs while preserving low-allocation hot paths for high-throughput workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Provide factory helpers: NewResponseFactory[T any](schema Schema) that returns typed constructors and validation hooks
StreamIngress API that hides retry/resume details and exposes a consumable chan/iterator with backpressure support
Examples: minimal CLI demo and unit tests showing streaming decode of nested JSON with typed structs and retry-on-failure semantics
Benchmarks comparing allocation/latency with previous ad-hoc decoding flow and showing <20% overhead in p99 under typical batch sizes
Documentation snippets in README + code example in examples/streaming-decode/
technical_notes: Design trade-off: prefer zero-copy where possible by decoding tokens into preallocated fields; fallback to json.Unmarshal for complex nested unknowns
Generics-based factory API to avoid reflection at call sites; use small reflection only during factory construction and cache builders for model types
StreamIngress will run a single goroutine that reads from the HTTP response body and emits typed events on a channel; consumer can opt-in to push-based callbacks instead
Retry semantics: on transient error (5xx, connection reset), StreamIngress will attempt N retries with exponential backoff and support resume tokens emitted by the model stream where available
Context semantics: cancellation cancels outstanding reads and drains channels gracefully; ensure no goroutine leaks by selecting on ctx.Done in decode loops
KV cache interaction: StreamIngress must expose a hook to populate the runtime KV cache for subsequent requests when streaming partial tokens that represent cached prefixes
Performance notes: microbenchmarks will include scenarios for small tokens (chat) and long tokens (token-by-token decode) and measure allocs/op
Compatibility: maintain plumbability to both REST streaming SSE and HTTP/2 gRPC streams; abstract transport behind a minimal interface (StreamReader)
